newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES - AUG 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES - AUG 4.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business weeklies. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
-- The National Bank of Greece, which has a branch in Sofia, said it was interested in taking part in the privatisation of Bulgaria's Post Bank, Hebros Bank and possibly Express Bank.

-- Vassil Filipov, director of the state gas monopolist Bulgargas, asked private firms in Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy to transfer their stakes to Bulgargas under a government decision to restore the 50 percent state participation in the joint venture.

Under a intergovernmental agreement between Bulgaria and Russia, only state firms could share Bulgaria's 50 percent stake in Topenergy. Filipov urged Multigroup, Overgas Inc, First Private Bank and Chimimport to transfer their stakes to Bulgargas.

-- Twelve Bulgarian commercial banks, six of them private, would service state budget accounts under a decision of the central bank and finance ministry from July 25. Central bank officials said the banks had been chosen on the basis of their financial indicators.
-- The Sofia Municipal Bank has extended credits worth eight billion levs to help mills buy grain from the new harvest, the bank's executive director Kiril Grigorov said.

-- The Central Service for Fighting Organised Crime last week arrested three former executive directors of the insolvent private Trade & Savings Bank (TSBank) on charges of granting uncollateralised credits worth of $45.2 million and 20 million marks. Nikolai Zlatev and Stefan Todorov were freed on bail, but Lyubomir Gibinski remained under arrest.

-- Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftochim posted a 33.4 billion lev loss for 1996 which had grown to 85 billion levs by the end of May this year, a report presented to Finance Minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to discuss amendments to the constitution in September which would allow foreigners to buy land, parliament speaker Yordan Sokolov said.
-- Bulgaria's Union of Tobacco Growers said it saw tobacco output for this year at 60,000 tonnes.
